# Candidate module designs
- Module-D3: large-area light guide with thin bonded dichroic filter.
- Module-D1: wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout.
- Module-D2: compact SiPM tile array.

# Thermal-cycling tests
Batches of 40 modules of each design were cycled 20 times between 300 K and 87 K.
Fraction failed (open channels or delamination):
- Module-D3: 30%  (the thin light-guide bonding cracks on cooldown)
- Module-D1: 2%
- Module-D2: 0.5%
Requirement: at most 5% failures after 20 cycles.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, 20% coverage)
Light collection: Module-D3 38 PE/MeV, Module-D1 27 PE/MeV, Module-D2 18 PE/MeV. It rises with coverage, roughly as coverage^0.8.

# Meeting notes 2026-01-20
Cabling feedthroughs were reviewed; enough feedthroughs are available for up to 30% coverage.

# Cryostat
Membrane cryostat; argon purity better than 100 ppt O2-equivalent is expected after recirculation.

content.text: D3 fails robustness. D1 is next best, at 30% coverage: 27×(1.5)^0.8 ≈ 37 PE/MeV.

input.justification: D3 has the highest light yield but 30% thermal-cycling failures, against a 5% limit. The modules can't be accessed after the cryostat is filled, so D3 is excluded. Of the remaining designs, D1 gives more light than D2 (27 vs 18 PE/MeV at 20% coverage) and passes thermal cycling at 2% failures. Light collection rises with coverage, so I chose the 30% maximum. Enough feedthroughs are available for 30%. The estimated yield is about 37 PE/MeV, from extrapolating the 2025 scaling of coverage^0.8. That is an extrapolation, not a direct simulation.

requirements.evidence: D1 is the highest-yield design that passes robustness. Its estimated yield at 30% coverage is about 37 PE/MeV, extrapolated from 27 PE/MeV at 20%.
